problem: Old code that the C2-1 fix did not touch. It falls in the case list the work named: a start in flight, at the same commit and at another. When the settle lock is held, _held_answer polls for a 'running' record and answers the first one it reads. It never compares that record's commit with this call's head, and it never probes the settle lock or the product lock again. _wait_for_running now does all three. (a) At another commit, a second start answers the old commit's product, where D14 says to replace it ('no demo runs old code'). Probe in a scratch copy: a first start in its settle window at head aaaa (SETTLE_SECONDS 1.5, env._head monkeypatched per thread) and a second start at head bbbb. The second returned exit 0 with the first's pid 86079, the record still said commit aaaa, and the old product was alive. (b) If the settling start call dies while a second start waits, the record stays 'starting' under a free settle lock. That is the stale case S3R-jobs-C1-2 handles on entry, but the loop waits out _STARTING_WAIT and fails. Probe: the _jobs_helper env-start call was killed 0.3 s into a second start's wait. The second returned 1, 'another start of this subject is still settling', after 5.12 s, with the orphaned product alive. The next start recovers. The same probes give the same results with this round's fix reverted, so the fix did not introduce this. test_start_joins_a_start_call_still_in_flight covers only the same commit.
proposed_resolution: Make the settle-held loop decide the way _wait_for_running does. On a fresh 'running' record, answer it only when its commit equals head; otherwise call stop_products(subject=...) and return None, so the caller takes the lock and starts. On each poll, if the settle lock is free and the record still says 'starting', take the stale path: stop_products(subject), then return None. If the product lock is free, return None. Add two tests to test_env.py. (1) A start in flight at another commit (env._head monkeypatched per thread) returns 0 with a new pid; the old product is gone and the record names the new commit. (2) The settling start call is killed while a second start waits; the second returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT and the orphan is gone.

problem: Old code that the C2-1 fix did not touch. It falls in the case list the work named: a start in flight, and a holder that exits without writing. When the product lock is held and the read after the probe finds no record, _held_answer returns None at once. start() then probes the lock a single time, without blocking, and returns 1, 'the product lock stays held'. Two kinds of holder reach this path: a start in flight that has taken the product lock but not yet written 'starting' (the first start of a new subject, or a start between port attempts after the failed attempt's record was unlinked), and a holder that exits without writing when no stale record is present. Probe A in a scratch copy: a first start with _launch delayed 1 s after taking the lock, then a second start. The second returned 1, 'the product lock stays held', in 0.01 s, while the first answered pid 85947. D14 says the second returns the first. Probe C: a holder held the lock for 0.8 s with no record. start returned 1 in 0.02 s. The same holder over a stale running record, in test_start_takes_the_lock_when_a_holder_exits_without_writing, gets 0. The case comment in test_env.py says case 1 'is waited for, then answered' and case 5 'frees the lock, which the waiting start takes'. Both hold only when a record is present. The same results come from the code with this round's fix reverted.
proposed_resolution: Treat a held lock with no usable record as a start in flight. Send _held_answer's last branch to the wait in _wait_for_running: answer a 'running' record whose group lives at the same commit, replace it at another, return None when the lock comes free, and fail after _STARTING_WAIT. Extend that wait so that a 'starting' record that appears under a held settle lock is waited on the same way. A lock held by a holder that escaped its group then fails after 5 s rather than at once, which is acceptable. Add two tests to test_env.py, each at the head commit and at another. (A) A start delayed between taking the lock and writing 'starting': the overlapping start returns 0 with the same pid (head commit), or with a new pid and the first product gone (another commit). (C) A holder with no record that exits after about 0.5 s: the start returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT. Correct the case comment so that it matches what is tested.
